perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- Ethan knows Gary Guo as a long-time close friend since middle school; Gary is a doctor.
- Ethan directly noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep.
- Ethan became concerned and invited Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation.
- Ethan heard Gary initially refuse, saying he appreciated the concern but could not go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work.
- Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than professional obligations.
- Ethan told Gary they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge.
- Ethan heard Gary say it was complicated and that he did not want to burden Ethan.
- Gary later opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities.
- Ethan heard Gary agree and say he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed his progress and challenges, and observed Gary making efforts to change.
- Gary told Ethan things were better, that he was less overwhelmed thanks to Ethan’s help, and that he had time for a movie.
- Ethan felt hopeful and proud, told Gary he was proud of his progress, and reminded Gary he was there whenever needed.
- After a year, Ethan observed Gary managing a healthier work-life balance and appearing capable on his own.
- Ethan told Gary he was always just a call away if needed, but that Gary had this.
- Gary thanked Ethan, said he could not have done it without Ethan’s support, and said he felt more in control.
- Ethan decided it was time to step back while remaining available if needed.
